verdicts.own_cite: docs/research/fidelity/MOTION_MEASUREMENTS.md:24 (verbatim `| Hit stagger | **12 frames total: 4 upright + 8 bent-forward** | duel-strike-A: frames 036–047 after streak | ...`) read against :18 `| Animation pose rate | **15fps** (pose steps every 4th video frame, strict)` and reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/EnemyShield.as:39 + :123-125
verdicts.reason: Every cite resolves, but the decomposition is wrong on two independent grounds. (a) ORDERING: EnemyZombie.gotHit() sets gotHitCounter = 12 at :522 and enters FLINCH_STATE at :544 in the SAME call, and both advance on the same per-NPC tick — EnemyShield.as:39 `mcs.updateAnimation()` then :123-125 `--gotHitCounter`, with MCSCharacter.updateAnimation() (:1315) advancing exactly one pose per call. So the 8-pose flinch is NESTED inside the 12-tick window (0-7 of 0-11), never '4 frames held THEN the 8-frame clip'. The recreation recipe the claim writes down is not what the source does. (b) UNITS: the '12' at MOTION_MEASUREMENTS.md:24 is VIDEO frames at 60fps (the same table's 'settled 20f ≈ 333ms' pins the rate), while :18 measures the pose latch at 15fps strict, so an 8-pose clip spans 32 video frames ≈ 533ms, not the 8 bent-forward video frames (133ms) it is matched to. 12 = 4 + 8 is arithmetic across three incommensurate clocks; 'triangulated across three independent artifacts' is exactly what it is not. The stagger half of (3) does die, but by enemies-ai/flinch-state-exists, not by this.

new_findings.text: REBUILD_READINESS.md's 'no 10th-rebirth tier' is FALSE in the shipped web build. Rebirth pays +25 heavenly gold normally and +100 when STAT_DAN == 8, and DAN increments only while < 9 — so the ceiling is DAN 9, which the game announces as rank DAN+1 = 10. MAX_DAN_RANK=10 (as displayed) and tenthGold=100 are therefore CONTRACT on v0.717, not INFERRED, and the wiki's 'kyudan/9th' datum was never garbled — it is the raw DAN ceiling. The film's flat +25 is true only because the player never reached DAN 8. The android build pays 5/20 instead, so 25/100 must be taken from the WEB file.

verdicts.own_cite: reference/extracted/android/98_MCSCharacter_UndeadAnimationData.bin — I decoded it and found <anim i="zom_stumble" d="39">, the clip EnemyZombie.as:285-286 plays for FLINCH_STATE. 4 + 39 != 12.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED as numerology across three unit spaces. (a) gotHitCounter=12 (NPC.as:462) is an i-frame WINDOW, not a lockout — proven by the packet's own claim gothitcounter-is-iframes, which I verified; a window that gates being-hit cannot 'decompose' into animation phases. (b) MOTION_MEASUREMENTS.md:24's '4 upright + 8 bent-forward' is VIDEO frames ('duel-strike-A: frames 036-047'), and the same table's line 18 fixes the pose latch at 15fps = one pose per 4 video frames; <anim d="8"> is 8 ANIMATION frames (MCSCharacter.updateAnimation advances frameCounter by 1 per tick against currentAnimationDuration). Summing them is unit-mixing. (c) Decisive: the flinch clip is NOT universally 8 frames — the zombie's is 39. (d) No code anywhere holds 4 frames before flinch; doFlinch() starts the anim on the same tick as the hit. Every cited artifact is real; the synthesis is not. OVERTURN REFUTED — :220's stagger half was already carried by flinch-state-exists; this claim adds a false 'fully CLOSED, not partial'.

It is consumed by the character sheet at InventoryUI.as:1937 and printed to the player at :2233 ('skill cooldown modifier: 0.' + int(mod*1000)). This closes skills-meters blocker ④ at REBUILD_READINESS.md:195 and the SPD half of progression blocker ① at :200.

new_findings.text: A limit the vector-art finding does not state, which would mislead a builder. Its fill histograms count entries in each shape's FILLSTYLEARRAY, so '#000000 x243' means 243 shape records DECLARE a black fill slot — not that black covers the most pixels. Rendered-area ranking would need edge records and shape geometry, which neither of us parsed. My independent parse of the same three files reproduces the ranking exactly and the mid-table counts exactly (#333333 x160, #CCCCCC x147, #FECA98 x127, #B78F6C x120 in 115; #30291D x35, #5A4D2E x33, #3A3323 x23, #251F16 x21, #453929 x21 in 120), which is why I judged the finding HELD — but the label matters.

new_findings.text: BUFF_ATTACK does not multiply damage by 1.5 - it multiplies the minDamage FLOOR by 1.5 and leaves damageRange untouched. Damage rolls as minDamage + random()*damageRange, so under the buff the expected damage rises by 1.5*minDamage - minDamage, i.e. strictly LESS than a 1.5x total unless damageRange is zero. Consequence for the contaminated duel_dense footage: it is inflated, but 'divide by 1.5' is the wrong correction and would under-report the true TTK. The same is true of BUFF_INJURED (x0.5 on minDamage and defense and baseSlashLength) and BUFF_DEFENSE (x1.5 on defense only).

new_findings.text: REBUILD_READINESS.md:115 says the world map is a 'sparse geographic Japan outline, not a grid you can generate from W×H'. The rendered board contradicts that: it is a regular rectangular lattice of uniform rounded-square tiles, and territories carry integer (x,y) coordinates — 'NAGANO (26,52)' — printed in the header. The Japan outline is a background painting drawn UNDER the lattice, not the board's geometry.
new_findings.quote: Header reads 'NAGANO (26,52)  LEVEL: 9'. Below it, uniform rounded-square tiles in strict rows and columns (I count 13-14 columns across five visible rows), each tile the same size and pitch, with a soft brown landmass shape painted behind and bleeding across tile borders — i.e. the coastline is wallpaper, the tiles are the board. One tile is highlighted with a white selection outline. Legend: 'VILLAGE  TOWN  CITY  CASTLE TOWN  DESTROYED  QUEST'.

new_findings.text: The web v0.717 damage function diverges from android and CONFIRMS the ledger's CRIT_MULT=1.3. reference/decompiled/shs3_payload/scripts/§1t99s0§.as:3255-3276 rolls baseDamage = minDamage + random()*damageRange, then applies LIGHT x(0.5 + 0.4*lightMastery*0.1), BALANCED x(1 + 0.2*balancedMastery*0.1), HEAVY/DUAL/REVERSED x1.4 - and then, only when reload == maxreload, returns 'dmg * 1.3 + STAT_CRITICALDMG' for EVERY stance, with no Light special case. Android (MCSPlayer.as:3198-3223) instead uses x1.2 non-Light / x1.5 Light and stance factor x1.5. Two consequences: the crit is DETERMINISTIC on a full Focus bar (no proc chance anywhere), and the ledger's wiki-sourced 'Critical = 1.3 x Physical' is now a CONTRACT code fact for the target build. At mastery 9 the web stance ceilings compute to 0.86 / 1.18 / 1.40, matching the ledger's §3.3 'the stance tables (dmg 0.9/1.2/1.4) are MASTERY-9 CEILING values'.

new_findings.text: In-combat stance switching in web v0.717 is FOCUS-GATED at a flat 48, not hard-locked - ledger §3 item 4 is wrong and the recreation's Focus-gated in-combat switch was right. reference/decompiled/shs3_payload/scripts/§1t99s0§.as:3050 returns 'canChangeStance() && reload >= 48'; :3060 opens nextStance with 'if(reload < 48) return;'; and :3160-3162, inside the StageManager battle predicate (structurally aligned with android's 'if(StageManager.isBattle())' at MCSPlayer.as:3096), charges 'reload -= 48'. So the switch IS permitted in battle, at a price of 48 Focus, and the 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE' HUD text is that Focus threshold firing - not an unconditional lock. Android uses a different rule entirely: gate at maxreload/6 = 20 (MCSPlayer.as:2977) and a graded cost (reload > max/2 -> set to max/3, else -= max/6; :3098-3105). Corroborated on film: the third bar in reference/frames/duel_dense/Nr4fQstqHDM_428.0.png (crop 230,960-560,1070 @4x LANCZOS) reads CANNOT CHANGE STANCE with no visible fill, which is exactly the reload <= 48 state that §1t113s0§.as:328 renders as scaleX 0.
new_findings.ledger_text: 4. **In-combat stance is HARD-LOCKED in v0.717** ("CANNOT CHANGE STANCE"). The recreation's Focus-gated in-combat switch models **removed 2014 behavior**. The *out-of-combat* switch costing Focus IS real; the *in-combat* switch is a recreation divergence — label it, don't present it as original.
new_findings.lane_impact: L-combat-core and L-skills-meters: the switch-cost third of blocker (3) 'Focus numerics (max/fill/switch-cost)' CLOSES at 48 for v0.717, and ledger §3 item 4 must be reversed - stop labelling the in-combat Focus switch a recreation divergence.

new_findings.text: What actually falls in ledger item 7. reference/decompiled/shs3_payload/scripts/§1t1523s0§.as:2644-2652 is 'if(getStat(DAN) == 8) { changeStat(§1t9413s0§,100); announce(...,"10"); } else { changeStat(§1t9413s0§,25); } if(getStat(DAN) < 9) { changeStat(DAN,1); }'. §1t9413s0§ is declared = 12 at §1t1523s0§.as:228 and android's STAT_HGOLD is 12 at StatsManager.as:194, so the currency is Heavenly Gold - which the game's own UI calls simply 'Gold'. Therefore: (a) a tenth-rebirth tier DOES exist, so 'film shows a flat +25 gold every rebirth, no 10th-rebirth tier' is false; (b) the DAN < 9 cap means dan ranks 0-9, i.e. exactly 10, so MAX_DAN_RANK=10 is now code-grade; (c) both config VALUES the ledger wanted demoted - tenthGold=100 and +25g - are exactly correct and should be promoted to CONTRACT, not demoted to INFERRED. Android v0.682 nerfs the same payout to 5 / 20 HGold (StatsManager.as:2201-2207) - do not carry those numbers over.
new_findings.ledger_text: 7. `MAX_DAN_RANK=10` and `tenthGold=100` should be INFERRED, not CONTRACT. The only wiki datum is garbled ("dan rank 5 (kyudan)" — kyudan=9th); film shows a **flat +25 gold** every rebirth, no 10th-rebirth tier.

new_findings.text: The live blade stroke's render contract is a TAPER, and it is a free on-screen readout of the reach cap. reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/InputManager.as:360 and reference/decompiled/shs3_payload/scripts/§1t1541s0§.as:360 are byte-identical: 'canvas.graphics.lineStyle(thickness - thickness * ((maxDistance - distanceLeft) / maxDistance), 10027008, 1, false, LineScaleMode.NONE, CapsStyle.ROUND, JointStyle.ROUND, 3);' with 'internal static var thickness:int = 8;' at :57 in both files. distanceLeft starts at maxDistance and counts down, so the stroke is drawn at 8 px where the player starts the line and thins linearly to 0 px exactly at the reach cap. The two NAMED styles greenLine() (0x009900) and redLine() (0x990000) are NOT the blade - my grep shows their only callers anywhere are SkillUI.as:75 and SkillUI.as:136, i.e. the vestigial gesture pad.
new_findings.quote: InputManager.as:360 — 'canvas.graphics.lineStyle(thickness - thickness * ((maxDistance - distanceLeft) / maxDistance),10027008,1,false,LineScaleMode.NONE,CapsStyle.ROUND,JointStyle.ROUND,3);' · :57 — 'internal static var thickness:int = 8;'
new_findings.lane_impact: L-art-anim-audio-feel and L-combat-core: the blade stroke is 8 px at the origin tapering to 0 px at the reach cap, colour 0x990000, ROUND caps and joins, miter 3 - a full render contract in one line, and a visual way to measure the reach cap off any longplay frame that shows a full-length stroke.

new_findings.text: Rider on the reach-per-stance close: use the WEB coefficients, not android's. reference/decompiled/shs3_payload/scripts/§1t99s0§.as:3094 sets LIGHT slashLength = baseSlashLength * 1.4; :3104 BALANCED = base * (1 + 0.2 * balancedMastery * 0.1); :3116-3120 HEAVY = base * (0.5 + 0.4 * heavyMastery * 0.1) floored at 100; :3131 REVERSED = base * 1.4; :3142-3146 DUAL = base floored at 100. Android instead uses x1.5 for LIGHT and REVERSED and a ·0.01 mastery scale (MCSPlayer.as:3029, :3042, :3053). The base function and stage are parity, so the SHAPE of the close is safe: §1t1523s0§.as:2347 'return int(120 + Math.floor(_loc2_ * param1 / (20 + param1)));' and §1t1523s0§.as:104 'public static var stageWidth:int = 800;'. Worked example for a fresh v0.717 character (SPD 1, DAN 0): base = 120 + floor(90*1/21) = 124 stage px, so LIGHT 173, BALANCED 124, HEAVY max(62,100) = 100 - and at 1920-wide capture that is x2.4 screen px per stage px.

new_findings.text: Corrected replacement for the refuted contamination claim. The 13-entry buff table is real and verifies exactly (reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/StatsManager.as:288-312; labels at OverworldHUD.as:1388-1425 - XP/DAMAGE/DEFENSE/SPEED 150%, AP-regen and duel-token-regen 200%), and the duel_dense footage IS buffed: I read reference/frames/duel_dense/Nr4fQstqHDM_428.0.png (crop 230,960-560,1070 @4x LANCZOS) and saw gold '150% DAMAGE' under the HUD bars. But the buff is applied as 'this.minDamage *= 1.5;' ONLY - reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/MCSPlayer.as:210-212, and web §1t99s0§.as:211-213 identical - while damageRange is untouched and getDamage rolls 'minDamage + Math.random() * damageRange' (MCSPlayer.as:3201). So the buff lifts the FLOOR of the damage roll, not the roll; dividing a measured damage or TTK by 1.5 is a systematic over-correction. The branches are an else-if chain, so exactly ONE buff is ever active. BUFF_INJURED is the mirror and has never been recorded anywhere: ':218-221 this.minDamage *= 0.5; this.defense *= 0.5; this.baseSlashLength *= 0.5;' - it halves REACH too.
new_findings.quote: MCSPlayer.as:210-212 — 'if(StatsManager.hasBuff(StatsManager.BUFF_ATTACK)) { this.minDamage *= 1.5; }' · :3201 — 'var baseDamage:int = this.minDamage + Math.random() * this.damageRange;' · :218-221 — 'else if(StatsManager.hasBuff(StatsManager.BUFF_INJURED)) { this.minDamage *= 0.5; this.defense *= 0.5; this.baseSlashLength *= 0.5;'
new_findings.lane_impact: All video-measurement lanes: flag reference/frames/duel_dense/ as BUFF_ATTACK-active, but do NOT divide by 1.5 - only minDamage is inflated, so a measured hit is (1.5*minDamage + roll), and the unbuffed floor is recoverable only if damageRange is known. L-items-equipment gains the 13-buff consumable layer plus the previously unrecorded BUFF_INJURED reach penalty.

new_findings.text: The WEB v0.717 build uses DIFFERENT per-stance reach multipliers from Android v0.682, so the reach model L1 must port is not the one the android decompile gives. Web: Light = base x1.4, Balanced = base x(1 + 0.2*balancedMastery*0.1), Heavy = base x(0.5 + 0.4*heavyMastery*0.1) with a hard floor of 100, Reversed = base x1.4, Dual = base x1.0 floor 100. Android: 1.5 / (1+0.5*m*0.01) / (0.5+0.5*m*0.01) / 1.5 / 1.0. At mastery 9 the balanced multiplier is 1.18 web against 1.045 android and heavy is 0.86 against 0.545. The SPD base term 120 + floor((90 + Dan*5)*spd/(20+spd)) IS identical in both builds (§1t1523s0§.as:2346-2347 vs StatsManager.as:1917-1918), and both feed InputManager.setMaxDistance, so only the multipliers diverge. new_findings.text: The open question behind the packet's hp-less-combat-rows claim is answerable and I answered it. Spawn level for combat NPCs comes from the QUEST WAVE, not from npcdata. NPCManager.as:110-131 reads wave[i].enemy[j].lvl into new NPCHolder(id,fatal,xpos,lvl); :407/411/433/437 pass npcHolder.getLvl() into createEnemy/createObjective, which call actor.setLevel(lvl) when lvl != 0 (:877-879, :931-934). 160 of the 169 <enemy> blocks in questdata.xml carry <lvl>. Concretely: Gojo Takamori npc 190 spawns at lvl 25 (questdata.xml:26101 id, :26105 lvl) and npc 191 at 35 (:25862 / :25866); Magoichi npc 188 at 35, npc 810 at 27. Friendlies never need one — FriendlyElite.as:70 and FriendlyArcher.as:58 call setLevel(StatsManager.getLevel()), so allies scale to the player, and 7 of the 12 skill-carrying hp-less rows are ai 30 / ai 34 = FriendlyElite / FriendlyArcher (NPCManager.as:608-621). NPC.setLevel at :239-259 then rescales damage, defense and maxhp by lvl/level and hard-clamps all three to 1 when lvl <= 10.

Combined with the quest-wave <lvl> rows this closes the spawn side of blocker ② for the 22 hp-less combat NPCs and gives blocker ① a real formula to test.

new_findings.text: The respawn third of the gather blocker is closed. Obj_OreDeposit.as:80-87 clearOre() calls StageManager.addToDeadList(objectName); StageManager.as:621-625 pushes the name onto roomDeadList, and GameStage.as:602-630 createRoomObjects suppresses any object whose name is in that list when the room is built. roomDeadList is emptied at StageManager.as:249 (initRooms) and :366 (node change). So a mined-out deposit repopulates the next time the node is entered — the respawn rule is 'per node visit', with the AP cost per swing as the only throttle. There is no timer and no server tick involved.

new_findings.text: There is a three-way stance counter-triangle worth x1.2 that the ledger's damage math does not carry. MCSPlayer.as:3701-3707: if (attacker Light vs defender Balanced) or (Balanced vs Heavy) or (Heavy vs Light), damage *= 1.2 — and it is applied BEFORE the physical defense subtraction at :3709 and before the min-damage floor at :3710-3713, so it compounds with everything downstream including the behead x1.5 at :3716. new_findings.text: The complete web v0.717 per-stance damage ladder, the crit rule and the Heavy defence penalty are all in one function and none of them are inferred: Light = base x (0.5 + 0.4 x lightMastery x 0.1) i.e. 0.5 -> 0.9; Balanced = base x (1 + 0.2 x balancedMastery x 0.1) i.e. 1.0 -> 1.2; Heavy, Dual and Reversed = base x 1.4 flat; at reload == maxreload the result is x1.3 plus the flat critical-damage stat; Heavy defence is x0.8. new_findings.text: The elemental ATK-vs-DEF formula is fully recovered, and nobody in this packet claimed it. Each element channel is mitigated independently by the matching elemental DEF, floored at 1 whenever the attacker carried any of that element (so an elemental hit always chips at least 1 per channel) and at 0 otherwise; the four channels are then summed with the physical damage into a single HP deduction. The defender's elemental DEF stats are themselves derived from the COUNTER element's ATK stat, which is the code-side form of the element wheel.

new_findings.text: slashLength / InputManager.maxDistance is an ARC-LENGTH budget for the drawn line, not a radial reach. InputManager.as:198 seeds distanceLeft = maxDistance on mouse-down; :353-367 subtracts Math.sqrt of each mouse-move segment's squared displacement along the drawn polyline, and the trail's line thickness tapers as ((maxDistance - distanceLeft) / maxDistance). Coordinates are game-stage space: (args.stageX - StatsManager.stageOffsetX) / StatsManager.stageScale. So the stance 'reach cap' caps HOW LONG A LINE YOU MAY DRAW in stage px, not how far the blade extends from the body. Any recreation that models it as a radius will feel wrong on curved and zig-zag slashes, and the ledger's close-path ('measure blade-FX tip-to-body span from footage') was asking for a different quantity from the one the code caps.

new_findings.text: The Focus/crit gating rule that REBUILD_READINESS.md lists as ABSENT in two separate blockers is fully specified in the source. The reload meter is 5*24 = 120 frames (5 s at 24 fps). It recharges +6 per tick, drains by slashUsage (x0.5 light / x1 / x1.5 heavy) per slash, is zeroed when a slash fires at full, is penalised on being hit (reload > max/2 collapses to max/3, else -max/6), gates stance switching below max/6, and drives the HUD bar by scaleX with the crit text appearing only at percentage >= 1.
